subject: POC Observability — evaluation schedule & dashboard map
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: James Mason <jmason@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's call (observability focus)

James — thanks for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and the recommended POC approach focused on observability so we can validate performance and operational fit. Core ask: let’s verify latency/throughput characteristics and make sure your SREs can reproduce key incidents from your test workloads.

High-level success criteria (proposal):
- P50 latency under 200ms for 512-token average requests; P95 under 450ms
- Error rate <0.5% (5xx/timeout) during standard load; tail reliability maintained under peak bursts
- Observability completeness: traces with end-to-end request IDs, token-level generation timing, and GPU utilization exported to your telemetry
- Ability to run a 48hr soak and a short 1hr spike test without functional regressions

Recommended scope for first 4 weeks:
1) Week 0 (access & baseline): credential exchange, test dataset ingest, baseline perf from your dev traffic
2) Week 1 (deploy & wire observability): deploy model variant, enable tracing, wire logs/metrics to BrightLeaf Datadog/BigQuery
3) Week 2 (load/shock tests): run concurrent sessions, cache-warmup scenarios, and collect dashboards
4) Week 3 (analysis & handoff): evaluate success criteria, collect export artifacts, and decide next steps

Owners (proposal):
- Redwood: Lauren (sales), Dev Patel (solutions lead), Jordan Blake (runtime eng)
- BrightLeaf: James Mason (POC lead), K. O'Neill (SRE)

Observability specifics we plan to surface (initial):
- End-to-end traces: request arrival -> token streaming -> completion; include request_id and model_variant
- Latency breakdowns: request queueing, kernel execution, token decode times (token-level percentiles)
- Throughput and concurrency: requests/sec, in-flight requests, avg session length
- Error and timeout logs: structured errors with model, route, and input signature
- Cache metrics: KV cache hit rate, prefix match coverage
- GPU metrics: GPU utilization, memory headroom, kernel stalls
- Cost proxies: tokens served, effective tokens/sec per GPU (for later optimization)

Attachments: brightleaf-poc-observability-plan.xlsx (plan rows + owners), redwood-dashboard-map.png (dashboard wireframe), poc-access-checklist.txt

Please confirm the above and the proposed timeline — if that looks good I’ll send the formal POC runbook and access checklist.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: James Mason <jmason@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@brightleaf.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC runbook + observability dashboard map (formal)

Team — attaching the formal runbook and a dashboard map image. Below is the canonical checklist and the concrete dashboards we’ll deliver by end of Week 2. I also added an access matrix.

Concrete deliverables (Week 2 wall):
- Dashboard: POC Overview (aggregate requests, success rate, p50/p95 latency)
- Dashboard: Token latency heatmap (token position vs. latency percentiles)
- Dashboard: Error inspector (errors by model variant, input checksum)
- Dashboard: Resource view (GPU utilization, memory, power draw if available)
- Tracing: Example end-to-end trace for a failed and successful request (sampled, linked to log line)
- Exports: Daily logs -> BigQuery (partitioned by date) + Datadog metrics (metric prefixes: redwood.poc.*)

Eval plan and acceptance tests (what we’ll run and how we’ll measure):
- Soak test: 48-hour steady-state at target traffic (TBD by BrightLeaf) — success: error rate <0.5%, SLOs met for >95% window
- Spike test: 1hr sudden 3x traffic burst — success: system recovers within 2 minutes with <1% request failure during recovery window
- Regression spot checks: we’ll validate semantic consistency on a small prompt set and surface any quality regressions (will include eval prompts and expected token counts)

Telemetry/implementation notes (Dev/Jordan action items):
- Tracing: instrument request_id through frontend -> inference runtime -> response; sample rate default 5% but adjustable to 100% for debugging windows
- Logs: structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms, error_code
- Metrics: redwood.poc.latency.p50/p95, redwood.poc.requests.count, redwood.poc.cache.hit_rate, redwood.poc.gpu.utilization
- Exports: set up Datadog API key (BrightLeaf to provide) and BigQuery sink for logs (service account key)

Next steps (timeline & asks):
- Today: BrightLeaf to provide Datadog API key, BigQuery dataset name, and allowlist IPs
- Wed (Day 2): Redwood to send SOW and DocuSign link for signature
- End of next week: baseline numbers and first dashboard alpha

I’ll mark Dev and Jordan as owners for the trace + log wiring. Monica will own dashboard construction and success criteria reporting. Rishi will lead the post-eval commercial sync.

— Lauren
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Quick notes from infra/runtime side:
- Firewall/IP allowlist: we need BrightLeaf’s egress IPs and Datadog key. If they want a VPC peering path we’ll need network contacts (can collect in the runbook)
- Tracing: Jordan will drop a tracing SDK snippet into the runtime today; we can enable 100% sampling for the first 4 hours of the spike test window to capture tail behavior
- KV cache metric: will emit redwood.poc.cache.hit_rate as a gauge every 30s; will also emit prefix_coverage as a tag

Plan to stand up a staging cluster (same instance types as production) for BrightLeaf tests — expecting ~6 hours of infra work once keys are in place.

— Dev
